SBLGNT:1Cor.12.25: 1 Cor 12:25 has members caring for one another (τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσι); a generic mutuality already carried on the page by Heb 10:24-25 and Gal 6:2; no distinct addition.
SBLGNT:1Cor.12.26: 1 Cor 12:26 (suffering and rejoicing together) is body-sympathy, not mutual transmission of truth or patience; Gal 6:2 and Eccl 4:10 make the kefil point more directly.
SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6: 1 Cor 13:6 says love rejoices with the truth; a love-hymn attribute, not an exchange of truth between people; Zech 8:16/Eph 4:25 serve paragraph 22.
SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7: 1 Cor 13:7 'bears all, endures all (ὑπομένει)' is said of love, not a community transmitting patience; too general beside Luke 8:15 and Col 3:13.
SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58: 1 Cor 15:58 'your labor is not empty in the Lord' restates the not-in-vain theme; 1 Cor 3:13-15 gives the sharper loss/remain contrast used for paragraph 12.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.13: 1 Cor 3:13: the day reveals each work by fire; context of the loss/wage contrast used in the counter-narrative to 18:103-105.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.14: 1 Cor 3:14: if the work remains (μενεῖ) the worker receives a wage; the positive half of the contrast in the annotation.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.15: 1 Cor 3:15: burnt work suffers loss (ζημιωθήσεται) while the worker himself is saved; differs from 18:105 where failed works leave their owners without weight.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.6: 1 Cor 3:6 one plants, another waters, God gives growth; supports the community-as-field image and its limit.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.8: 1 Cor 3:8 planter and waterer are one, each receives his own wage; part of the field passage quoted.
SBLGNT:1Cor.3.9: 1 Cor 3:9 'God's co-workers; God's field' is the quoted line resonating with the continuous pasture image.
SBLGNT:1Cor.9.10: 1 Cor 9:10 (ploughman ploughs in hope of a share) is about apostolic support; Deut 24:15 and Matt 20:8 carry the evening wage more exactly.
SBLGNT:1Cor.9.25: 1 Cor 9:25 (athlete's self-control for a crown) concerns ἐγκράτεια, not ṣabr's restraint of lament; Prov 16:32 is the closer Hebrew Bible formulation.
SBLGNT:1Cor.9.9: 1 Cor 9:9 quotes the unmuzzled ox of Deut 25:4 for apostolic wages; no specific contribution to the wage-of-work paragraph beyond Deut 24:15.
SBLGNT:1John.3.17: 1 John 3:17 condemns closing one's heart to a needy brother; a charity motif, not the debt/right sense of ḥaqq discussed in paragraph 23.
SBLGNT:1John.3.18: 1 John 3:18 'love in deed and truth' pairs work and truth but within love language; Zech 8:16 gives the reciprocal truth-speaking directly.
SBLGNT:1John.3.23: 1 John 3:23 pairs believing with loving one another; a faith+mutuality formula but without work or patience; 1 Thess 1:3 was chosen for paragraph 2.
SBLGNT:1Pet.2.20: 1 Pet 2:20 enduring while doing good is close to paragraph 37, but Jer 20:8-9 shows the cost of speaking truth more specifically.
SBLGNT:1Pet.3.15: 1 Pet 3:15 (ready defence of hope) is apologetic; 2 Tim 2:24-25 addresses transmitting truth without quarrel more directly.
SBLGNT:1Pet.3.20: 1 Pet 3:20 (few, eight souls saved through water) restates the flood exception; the Hebrew Gen 7:23 was quoted instead.
SBLGNT:1Pet.3.9: 1 Pet 3:9 (bless instead of returning insult) parallels 41:34, but Prov 25:21 and Rom 12:20-21 were used as the text and its reading.
SBLGNT:1Pet.4.19: 1 Pet 4:19 entrusting the soul to a faithful creator while doing good; not mutual patience among believers; no distinct addition.
SBLGNT:1Thess.1.3: 1 Thess 1:3 'work of faith, labour of love, endurance of hope' gathers faith, work and patience as nouns in genitive chains; quoted at paragraph 2.
SBLGNT:1Thess.5.11: 1 Thess 5:11 'encourage one another and build one another' is mutual exhortation, already represented by Heb 10:24-25 and Heb 3:13.
SBLGNT:1Thess.5.14: 1 Thess 5:14 'be patient toward all' is one-directional patience; Col 3:13's reciprocal participle fits paragraph 33 better.
SBLGNT:1Tim.6.11: 1 Tim 6:11 lists righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance; a virtue list without the reciprocal verbs; adds nothing beyond 1 Thess 1:3.
SBLGNT:1Tim.6.18: 1 Tim 6:18 (rich in good works, generous) is a wealth ethic; the lasting-works point is carried by Matt 6:20 and Peah 1:1.
SBLGNT:1Tim.6.19: 1 Tim 6:19 (good foundation stored for the future) duplicates the treasure image of Matt 6:20 used at paragraph 14.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.16: 2 Cor 4:16 inner renewal while the outer self wastes; a different anthropology than lasting works; not used.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.17: 2 Cor 4:17 light affliction producing a weight of glory; a reward-for-suffering motif without the heap/measure image of paragraph 35.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.18: 2 Cor 4:18 seen things temporary, unseen eternal; general contrast, weaker than Matt 6:20 for paragraph 14.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.7: 2 Cor 4:7 treasure in clay vessels; the vessel image concerns fragility, not the rim that holds contents in paragraph 30.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.8: 2 Cor 4:8 pressed but not crushed; a hardship catalogue that does not use a restraint or holding term; no specific addition.
SBLGNT:2Cor.4.9: 2 Cor 4:9 struck down but not destroyed; hardship catalogue only; no specific addition.
SBLGNT:2Cor.5.10: 2 Cor 5:10 judgment according to deeds duplicates Rom 2:6, which was chosen because 2:7 adds endurance in good work.
SBLGNT:2Cor.8.13: 2 Cor 8:13 relief without burdening the givers concerns a collection; not the ḥaqq-as-due relation; no addition.
SBLGNT:2Cor.8.14: 2 Cor 8:14 abundance supplying lack for equality; a resource-sharing motif rather than mutual reminding of what is owed.
SBLGNT:2John.1.4: 2 John 4 'walking in truth' is a conduct idiom; no exchange of truth between persons.
SBLGNT:2John.1.5: 2 John 5 love one another as the command from the beginning; reciprocity in love, not in counsel; no addition.
SBLGNT:2John.1.6: 2 John 6 love as walking in the commands; no reciprocal transmission; no addition.
SBLGNT:2Pet.1.5: 2 Pet 1:5 adds virtue to faith in a ladder; the chained sequence differs from the ayah's four verbs and adds no point beyond 1 Thess 1:3.
SBLGNT:2Pet.1.6: 2 Pet 1:6 self-control and endurance in the ladder; endurance appears but not as mutual counsel.
SBLGNT:2Pet.1.7: 2 Pet 1:7 brotherly affection and love close the ladder; no specific contribution.
SBLGNT:2Pet.2.17: 2 Pet 2:17 waterless springs as false teachers; the image concerns deception, not the rain-to-pasture scene; weak.
SBLGNT:2Thess.1.3: 2 Thess 1:3 faith grows and love for one another increases; mutuality of love, no transmission of truth or patience.
SBLGNT:2Thess.1.4: 2 Thess 1:4 endurance and faith in persecutions; the faith-endurance pair is already represented by 1 Thess 1:3 and Heb 10:36.
SBLGNT:2Tim.1.14: 2 Tim 1:14 'guard the good deposit' could illustrate the trust of 33:72, but 2 Tim 2:2 (deposit passed to trustworthy people) was used at paragraph 18 instead.
SBLGNT:2Tim.2.2: 2 Tim 2:2 entrust what you heard to faithful people who will teach others; chain of transmission and the double sense of πιστός.
SBLGNT:2Tim.2.24: 2 Tim 2:24 the Lord's servant must not quarrel; separates transmitting truth from contention.
SBLGNT:2Tim.2.25: 2 Tim 2:25 correcting opponents in gentleness toward knowledge of truth; completes the annotation's point.
SBLGNT:2Tim.3.10: 2 Tim 3:10 lists teaching, conduct, faith, patience, love, endurance; another virtue list, no added point.
SBLGNT:2Tim.4.2: 2 Tim 4:2 preach, reprove, exhort with all patience; close to the truth+patience pairing but 2:24-25 makes the anti-quarrel point used.
SBLGNT:2Tim.4.3: 2 Tim 4:3 heaping up teachers to suit desires resembles transmitting error (51:53) only loosely; not used.
SBLGNT:2Tim.4.7: 2 Tim 4:7 kept the faith, finished the race; a retrospective claim, no patience-promise grounding.
SBLGNT:2Tim.4.8: 2 Tim 4:8 crown of righteousness on that day; reward motif already covered by Rom 2:6-7.
SBLGNT:3John.1.3: 3 John 3 brothers testify to your truth; walking-in-truth idiom, no reciprocal counsel.
SBLGNT:3John.1.5: 3 John 5 'you do faithfully whatever you work for the brothers' (πιστὸν ποιεῖς) is a faith+work phrase but too incidental for paragraph 10.
SBLGNT:Acts.2.42: Acts 2:42 devotion to teaching and fellowship describes communal life, not mutual exhortation; no specific addition.
SBLGNT:Acts.2.44: Acts 2:44 believers holding all things in common is a property-sharing motif, not ḥaqq as due.
SBLGNT:Acts.2.45: Acts 2:45 distribution according to need; property-sharing motif; not used.
SBLGNT:Acts.4.32: Acts 4:32 one heart and soul of the believers; communal unity, but the page's point is reciprocal verbs; not used.
SBLGNT:Acts.4.34: Acts 4:34 no needy person among them; charity outcome, not the mutual reminding of what is owed.
SBLGNT:Acts.4.35: Acts 4:35 proceeds distributed by need; same property-sharing motif; not used.
SBLGNT:Col.1.10: Col 1:10 bearing fruit in every good work; generic fruit-of-works language, weaker than Ps 1:3-4.
SBLGNT:Col.1.11: Col 1:11 strengthened for all endurance and patience; not reciprocal; Col 3:13 used instead.
SBLGNT:Col.3.13: Col 3:13 ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων: reciprocal forbearance rendered with the reflexive pronoun, compared with sâbirû in 3:200.
SBLGNT:Col.3.16: Col 3:16 teaching and admonishing one another in psalms; mutual instruction, but Heb 10:24-25 was chosen for paragraph 19.
SBLGNT:Eph.2.10: Eph 2:10 created for good works; the faith/works relation is represented on the page through the two readings of Gen 15:6 (Rom 4; Jas 2).
SBLGNT:Eph.2.8: Eph 2:8 saved by grace through faith; proposed as a contrast to faith+works, but the page presents the Pauline position via Rom 4:3-5, which reads Gen 15:6 directly.
SBLGNT:Eph.2.9: Eph 2:9 'not from works' duplicates the Pauline contrast already given through Rom 4:4-5; no separate block.
SBLGNT:Eph.4.14: Eph 4:14 tossed by winds of teaching resembles the scattering paths of 6:153 loosely; not used.
SBLGNT:Eph.4.15: Eph 4:15 speaking the truth in love so that the body grows; context of the joint image in the annotation.
SBLGNT:Eph.4.16: Eph 4:16 the body fitted together through every joint (ἁφή); compared with ḥaqq as the meeting place of two bones.
SBLGNT:Eph.4.2: Eph 4:2 bearing with one another with patience (μακροθυμία); cited beside Col 3:13.
SBLGNT:Eph.4.25: Eph 4:25 quotes Zech 8:16 and grounds truth-speaking in being members of one another; Christian reading of the Zechariah text.
SBLGNT:Eph.6.14: Eph 6:14 belt of truth in the armour list; a defensive image, not the thrown/penetrating ḥaqq of paragraph 25; Heb 4:12 used instead.
SBLGNT:Gal.5.22: Gal 5:22 fruit of the Spirit list incl. patience and faithfulness; list without the reciprocal structure; no addition.
SBLGNT:Gal.5.6: Gal 5:6 faith working through love; faith+activity formula, but the page covers the faith/works relation via Gen 15:6 readings.
SBLGNT:Gal.6.1: Gal 6:1 restoring the one who errs in gentleness; first step of the sequence cited.
SBLGNT:Gal.6.2: Gal 6:2 'bear one another's burdens' quoted for the community standing for one another.
SBLGNT:Gal.6.9: Gal 6:9 not growing weary in doing good; completes the sequence cited.
SBLGNT:Heb.10.23: Heb 10:23 the promiser is faithful; grounds patience in the promise, as 40:55/30:60 ground sabr in the truth of the promise.
SBLGNT:Heb.10.24: Heb 10:24 consider one another to stir up love and good works; reciprocal exhortation quoted.
SBLGNT:Heb.10.25: Heb 10:25 not abandoning the assembly but encouraging (παρακαλοῦντες); quoted.
SBLGNT:Heb.10.36: Heb 10:36 'you need endurance' introduces the Habakkuk quotation; quoted.
SBLGNT:Heb.10.38: Heb 10:38 quotes Hab 2:4 (Greek form) 'my righteous one shall live by faith'; the Christian reading of the Habakkuk text.
SBLGNT:Heb.11.1: Heb 11:1 faith as assurance of things hoped; a definition of faith in hope terms, not the trust/security or affirmation sense developed on the page.
SBLGNT:Heb.11.17: Heb 11:17 Abraham's faith tested in offering Isaac; the page's Abraham paragraph concerns fear and security (Gen 15), not the binding.
SBLGNT:Heb.11.22: Heb 11:22 Joseph's dying instruction about his bones; deathbed charge content is burial, as in Gen 50:25; Gen 49 was used for the contrast.
SBLGNT:Heb.11.8: Heb 11:8 Abraham obeys by faith and departs; faith-as-action, not the security theme of paragraph 6.
SBLGNT:Heb.12.1: Heb 12:1 run the race with endurance; athletic endurance, no restraint image; not used.
SBLGNT:Heb.12.11: Heb 12:11 discipline painful now, later yields peaceful fruit; matches the bitter-medicine image of paragraph 31.
SBLGNT:Heb.12.2: Heb 12:2 Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before him; christological, no grounding of patience in the truth of a promise beyond Heb 10:36-38.
SBLGNT:Heb.3.13: Heb 3:13 exhort one another every day lest hardened; cited in the mutual exhortation annotation.
SBLGNT:Heb.4.12: Heb 4:12 the word sharper than a two-edged sword, piercing to joints and marrow; resonates with the penetrating thrust named from ḥqq.
SBLGNT:Heb.6.10: Heb 6:10 God not unjust to forget your work; reward-for-work motif already carried by Deut 24:15 and Matt 20:8.
SBLGNT:Heb.6.11: Heb 6:11 diligence to the full assurance of hope; no added point.
SBLGNT:Heb.6.12: Heb 6:12 imitate those who through faith and patience inherit promises; close to paragraph 36 but Heb 10:36-38 carries the same pairing with the Habakkuk text.
SBLGNT:Heb.6.18: Heb 6:18 those who fled for refuge (καταφυγόντες) to grasp hope; refuge image for paragraph 5.
SBLGNT:Heb.6.19: Heb 6:19 hope as a secure and firm anchor of the soul; quoted with 6:18.
SBLGNT:Jas.1.22: Jas 1:22 be doers of the word not hearers only; a hearing/doing motif not tied to loss of works; not used.
SBLGNT:Jas.1.3: Jas 1:3 testing of faith produces endurance; faith-endurance pair, no restraint sense; not used.
SBLGNT:Jas.1.4: Jas 1:4 let endurance have its complete work; no specific contribution beyond Luke 8:15.
SBLGNT:Jas.2.17: Jas 2:17 faith without works is dead; the Jacobean position is given through 2:21-23, which read Gen 15:6 directly.
SBLGNT:Jas.2.22: Jas 2:22 faith worked together with Abraham's works; quoted as the reading of Gen 15:6 opposite Rom 4.
SBLGNT:Jas.2.24: Jas 2:24 justified by works and not by faith only; the same position as 2:22-23; folded into the Gen 15:6 annotation without a separate quote.
SBLGNT:Jas.3.17: Jas 3:17 wisdom peaceable and full of good fruits; general, not the salāḥ/fasād pair.
SBLGNT:Jas.3.18: Jas 3:18 fruit of righteousness sown in peace; peace-making motif, weaker than Peah 1:1 used at paragraph 14.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.10: Jas 5:10 prophets as examples of suffering and patience; Jer 20:8-9 gives the prophetic cost of truth in the prophet's own words.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.11: Jas 5:11 Job's endurance; a figure of patience but no restraint-of-lament wording; not used.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.19: Jas 5:19 turning back one who wandered from the truth; close to tavsiye bi'l-ḥaqq but 2 Tim 2:24-25 was used for the non-quarrel point.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.20: Jas 5:20 restoring a sinner saves a soul; consequence of correction; not used.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.4: Jas 5:4 withheld wages cry out; inverse of Deut 24:15; Deut 24:15 was quoted directly.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.7: Jas 5:7 farmer waits patiently for early and late rain; waiting image, but Lam 3:26 links waiting to silence/restraint.
SBLGNT:Jas.5.8: Jas 5:8 be patient, establish your hearts; no added point.
SBLGNT:John.15.12: John 15:12 love one another; reciprocal love command without counsel; no addition.
SBLGNT:John.15.4: John 15:4 branch must remain in the vine to bear fruit; abiding motif, not lasting works; not used.
SBLGNT:John.15.5: John 15:5 vine and branches; organic unity image weaker than 1 Cor 3:6-9 for the joined pasture.
SBLGNT:Jude.1.12: Jude 12 waterless clouds as false teachers; deception image; not used.
SBLGNT:Luke.21.19: Luke 21:19 'by your endurance gain your souls' links patience to the escape from loss; quoted.
SBLGNT:Luke.6.35: Luke 6:35 love enemies and lend expecting nothing; close to 41:34 but Prov 25:21/Rom 12:21 were used as text and reading.
SBLGNT:Luke.6.38: Luke 6:38 good measure pressed down returned; a measure image, but the page's point is a heap without measure (subra); weak.
SBLGNT:Luke.8.13: Luke 8:13 rootless hearers fall away in the time of testing; context cited with 8:15.
SBLGNT:Luke.8.14: Luke 8:14 choked by cares and riches; context only, no holding/endurance wording.
SBLGNT:Luke.8.15: Luke 8:15 hold fast (κατέχουσιν) and bear fruit in endurance; ṣabr as holding.
SBLGNT:Mark.8.35: Mark 8:35 saving/losing life is context for 8:36, whose gain/loss wording was quoted; no separate block.
SBLGNT:Mark.8.36: Mark 8:36 gain the whole world and forfeit (ζημιωθῆναι) one's soul; loss/gain vocabulary beside the exception paragraph.
SBLGNT:Matt.10.22: Matt 10:22 the one who endures to the end will be saved; same point as Luke 21:19 which was quoted.
SBLGNT:Matt.11.28: Matt 11:28 rest for the burdened; burden relief by Jesus, not the capacity limit of 6:152; not used.
SBLGNT:Matt.11.30: Matt 11:30 easy yoke, light burden; resembles 'no soul beyond capacity' but Exod 18:18-22 shows the burden measure inside a community.
SBLGNT:Matt.16.27: Matt 16:27 repaid according to deeds; same as Rom 2:6 which was chosen.
SBLGNT:Matt.18.15: Matt 18:15 reprove a brother to gain him; correction procedure; 2 Tim 2:24-25 used for paragraph 26.
SBLGNT:Matt.18.16: Matt 18:16 witnesses accompany correction; procedural, no addition.
SBLGNT:Matt.20.12: Matt 20:12 full-day workers protest equal pay; the difference in measure noted in the annotation.
SBLGNT:Matt.20.13: Matt 20:13 the agreed denarius; part of the wage dispute summarized.
SBLGNT:Matt.20.15: Matt 20:15 the owner's generosity; the wage is measured by goodness, summarized in the annotation.
SBLGNT:Matt.20.8: Matt 20:8 when evening came the workers are called and paid; the evening wage scene quoted.
SBLGNT:Matt.24.12: Matt 24:12 love grows cold through lawlessness; no counterpart to transmitting error (51:53).
SBLGNT:Matt.24.13: Matt 24:13 endurance to the end brings salvation; duplicates Luke 21:19.
SBLGNT:Matt.25.35: Matt 25:35 feeding the hungry; resembles 90:14 but the page's paragraph is about mutual counsel of mercy; Zech 7:9 used.
SBLGNT:Matt.25.40: Matt 25:40 deeds for the least counted as for the king; not about mutual counsel.
SBLGNT:Matt.5.16: Matt 5:16 good works seen by others; display of works, not their loss; not used.
SBLGNT:Matt.5.44: Matt 5:44 love enemies; close to 41:34 but Rom 12:20-21 (reading Prov 25:21) was used.
SBLGNT:Matt.6.12: Matt 6:12 forgive our debts as we forgive our debtors; debt metaphor of sin; Rom 13:8 fits mutual obligation better.
SBLGNT:Matt.6.20: Matt 6:20 treasure where neither moth nor rust consume; the time-erosion contrast of paragraph 14.
SBLGNT:Matt.6.4: Matt 6:4 reward for hidden alms; not a wage-for-work scene.
SBLGNT:Matt.7.21: Matt 7:21 not everyone saying 'Lord' enters; word/deed contrast, not loss of works; not used.
SBLGNT:Matt.7.24: Matt 7:24 hearing and doing builds on rock; the building image could match the well-lining of paragraph 10 but is a hearing/doing parable; not used.
SBLGNT:Matt.7.25: Matt 7:25 the house on rock withstands storm; context of 7:24; not used.
SBLGNT:Matt.7.26: Matt 7:26 hearing without doing builds on sand; collapse image, but the page's loss paragraph is better served by 1 Cor 3:15.
SBLGNT:Phil.4.9: Phil 4:9 practise what you learned and received from me; transmission, but 2 Tim 2:2 shows the chain explicitly.
SBLGNT:Rev.12.11: Rev 12:11 not loving life unto death; martyr motif beside 7:126 but no restraint/vessel image.
SBLGNT:Rev.14.12: Rev 14:12 endurance of those keeping commands and faith; faith-endurance pair; no added point.
SBLGNT:Rev.2.10: Rev 2:10 be faithful unto death; martyr faithfulness; not used.
SBLGNT:Rev.2.19: Rev 2:19 works, love, faith, service, endurance; another list; no added point.
SBLGNT:Rev.2.2: Rev 2:2 works, labour and endurance; list without reciprocal verbs; no addition.
SBLGNT:Rev.2.3: Rev 2:3 endurance and not growing weary; no restraint wording.
SBLGNT:Rev.2.4: Rev 2:4 abandoned first love; contrast within a letter; not used.
SBLGNT:Rev.20.12: Rev 20:12 dead judged by deeds written in books; duplicates Rom 2:6 for paragraph 27.
SBLGNT:Rev.22.12: Rev 22:12 wage with me to give each according to work; duplicates Rom 2:6.
SBLGNT:Rev.3.19: Rev 3:19 those I love I reprove; divine reproof, not mutual counsel.
SBLGNT:Rom.12.12: Rom 12:12 enduring in affliction, cited in the reading of Prov 25:21 as the patience in the same chapter.
SBLGNT:Rom.12.20: Rom 12:20 quotes Prov 25:21-22 on feeding an enemy; the Christian reading of the Proverbs text.
SBLGNT:Rom.12.21: Rom 12:21 overcome evil with good; quoted beside 41:34.
SBLGNT:Rom.13.8: Rom 13:8 owe nothing except to love one another; mutual debt contrasted with ḥaqq as due.
SBLGNT:Rom.15.1: Rom 15:1 the strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak; close to the kefil image but one-directional; Gal 6:2 used.
SBLGNT:Rom.2.5: Rom 2:5 storing up wrath for the day; context of 2:6-7 only.
SBLGNT:Rom.2.6: Rom 2:6 render to each according to works; quoted for the day of ḥāqqa.
SBLGNT:Rom.2.7: Rom 2:7 to those who by endurance in good work seek glory, eternal life; joins patience and good work.
SBLGNT:Rom.2.8: Rom 2:8 wrath for those disobeying the truth; context of 2:6-7; no separate addition.
SBLGNT:Rom.4.4: Rom 4:4 the worker's wage reckoned as debt not grace; part of Paul's reading of Gen 15:6 quoted.
SBLGNT:Rom.4.5: Rom 4:5 faith of the one who does not work reckoned as righteousness; the Pauline side of the Gen 15:6 debate.
SBLGNT:Rom.5.3: Rom 5:3 affliction produces endurance; causal chain, not restraint; not used.
SBLGNT:Rom.5.4: Rom 5:4 endurance produces character and hope; not used.
SBLGNT:Rom.5.5: Rom 5:5 love poured into hearts; pouring image resembles 7:126 'pour patience on us' but the object is love, not patience; noted, not used.
SBLGNT:Rom.8.25: Rom 8:25 waiting with endurance for the unseen; waiting motif, Lam 3:26 preferred for the silence/restraint link.
SBLGNT:Titus.2.2: Titus 2:2 sound in faith, love, endurance; virtue list for elders; no added point.
Bava Metzia 30b: Bava Metzia 30b (opened as SEFARIA:Bava_Metzia.30b) reads Exod 18:20 'which they shall do' as going beyond the line of the law and blames Jerusalem's fall on insisting on strict law; a rich text, but it concerns legal strictness versus equity, not mutual counsel of ḥaqq; not used.
Makkot 24a: Makkot 24a (SEFARIA:Makkot.24a) reduces the 613 commandments to lists of eleven, six, three, two and finally Habakkuk's one, 'the righteous shall live by his faith'; a rabbinic short catalogue of the saving life.
